memory_versions.text:
Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Prior records were repeatedly rejected because multiple fields were invalid; retries sometimes reduced errors but did not resolve them. Do not resubmit unchanged data.
- Treat handwritten, phone, emailed, and partner-portal transcriptions as potentially unreliable. Extract and validate each field independently against the source.
- Preserve the customer’s exact full name and email; do not infer or “correct” names from the front-desk sender or nearby text.
- Normalize order_date consistently to the expected format; changing between ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and slash format alone did not ensure validity.
- Check priority, qty, and ship_country explicitly before submission; these appear to be frequent sources of rejection.
- Review every required field for missing, truncated, malformed, or misplaced values. The displayed source text may be clipped, so avoid filling fields from incomplete fragments.
- Use each attempt to diagnose and correct specific invalid fields. After three failed attempts, stop and let the record proceed to manual review rather than guessing.

Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source/transcription text is often clipped or unreliable, especially voicemail, email pastes, and partner/front-desk forwarding. Extract each field independently; never complete truncated values by inference.
- Preserve the customer’s exact full name and email from the source. Do not substitute the front-desk sender’s name or “correct” a partially visible name.
- Validate all six fields before submission, with particular scrutiny on priority, qty, and ship_country; repeated rejections commonly involve two fields, and changing only one field may leave another invalid.
- Do not trust front-desk labels such as “ordinary priority” as a complete or authoritative field value. Confirm the actual form/source value and allowed format.
- Normalize order_date to the expected format, but recognize that formatting alone does not establish validity; verify the date value and every other field.
- Do not resubmit unchanged data. After each rejection, diagnose all indicated invalid fields and correct only with evidence from the source; keep valid fields unchanged.
- Apparent repeated records may have different batch IDs, but do not assume forwarded notes or duplicate-check claims establish validity.
- If any required value is missing, malformed, misplaced, or unreadable, do not guess. Request clarification or send to manual review.
- After three failed attempts, stop; the record proceeds to manual review. Repeated attempts with partial or speculative corrections waste attempts.

Order intake lessons:
- Form versions 1 and 2 require exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Check the active version, but do not assume version 2 changes field requirements.
- Source/transcription text is often clipped or unreliable, especially voicemail, emailed pastes, handwriting, and partner/front-desk forwarding. Extract each field independently; never infer truncated or unreadable values.
- Preserve the customer’s exact full name and email from the source. Do not substitute a receptionist/front-desk sender or “correct” a partial name.
- Validate all six fields before submission. Rejections frequently involve two or more fields; correcting one field or resubmitting the same payload does not help.
- Treat front-desk descriptions such as “ordinary priority” or “marked ordinary” as unverified labels. Confirm the source value and the form’s allowed format. A priority of “0” was invalid.
- Normalize order_date only when the complete source value is available. Formatting alone does not prove validity; truncated dates (for example, an incomplete month) must not be submitted.
- After rejection, diagnose every indicated invalid field and correct only with source evidence; retain verified valid fields unchanged. Never resubmit unchanged data.
- Batch IDs, duplicate-check claims, and forwarding context do not establish validity or necessarily indicate a distinct record. Repeated submissions of the same invalid data across batches can exhaust attempts.
- If any required value is missing, malformed, misplaced, or unreadable, request clarification or use manual review rather than guessing.
- After three failed attempts, stop; the record proceeds to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1 and v2 require exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Verify the active version; do not assume v2 changes requirements.
- Source/transcription text is frequently clipped or unreliable, including voicemail, emailed pastes, handwriting, portal forwards, and reception transcriptions. Extract fields independently; never infer unreadable or truncated values.
- Preserve the customer’s exact full name and email from the source. Do not replace them with a receptionist/forwarder, expand a partial name, or treat repeated similar names/emails as proof of a distinct record.
- Validate all six fields before submission. A payload may have multiple invalid fields; fixing one or resubmitting unchanged data is ineffective. Rejections of two fields can later become four when more values are supplied incorrectly.
- Front-desk statements such as “duplicate check done,” “new,” “customer confirmed,” or “ordinary priority” are context, not source evidence. Confirm each value and the form’s allowed format; “0” priority was invalid.
- Normalize order_date only when the complete source value is available. A well-formatted or plausible date does not establish validity; missing, truncated, or null dates require clarification/manual review.
- After rejection, diagnose every indicated invalid field. Correct only fields supported by source evidence; retain verified valid fields unchanged. Never submit null, guessed, or reception-derived values.
- Batch IDs, forwarding routes, and repeated submissions do not establish validity or a new record. Track the underlying record across batches and avoid consuming attempts with the same incomplete payload.
- If any required value is missing, malformed, misplaced, or unreadable, request clarification or use manual review rather than guessing.
- After three failed attempts, stop; the record proceeds to manual review.
